title: Tepotinib monotherapy
context_label: Advanced MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC · after prior systemic therapy
scope_note: NCCP 00823a covers tepotinib on its own for adults with advanced non-small cell lung cancer carrying a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping change, after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy. It is not a first-line or adjuvant treatment guide.
schedule_summary: The usual starting dose is 450 mg once daily: two 225 mg tablets taken together with food. Treatment is continuous, without a planned rest week, while it is helping. Follow your prescribed dose; the team may use one 225 mg tablet or pause treatment for side effects.
purpose: Tepotinib blocks the MET growth signal in selected lung cancers with a MET exon 14 skipping change. In advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer and its symptoms. The tumour test and previous treatment help determine whether it is suitable.
indication_text: NCCP 00823a covers tepotinib on its own for adults with advanced non-small cell lung cancer carrying a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping change, after immunotherapy and/or platinum chemotherapy. It is not a first-line or adjuvant treatment guide.
administration_text: Take at the same time each day with food and swallow whole. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Do not double a dose. Ask your pharmacist if the timing is uncertain or if you vomit; do not take a replacement without advice. If swallowing is difficult, ask about the approved water-dispersion method.
monitoring_summary: Confirm the MET result, previous treatment, dose, other medicines and emergency contact. Check blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver function; ECG if clinically indicated. Discuss pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding, and perform a pregnancy test when applicable. Repeat blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver tests at the team’s agreed reviews. ECG is used when clinically indicated. Report new lung symptoms, swelling, diarrhoea or vomiting between visits. A rise in creatinine needs assessment because the medicine can change the test result without necessarily damaging the kidneys. Scans follow the Consultant’s plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Tepotinib
agents.explanation: Tepotinib inhibits the MET receptor. A MET exon 14 skipping change can keep this growth signal active; blocking it can slow or shrink selected lung cancers.
agents.watch: Report new cough or breathlessness, swelling, severe bowel symptoms, jaundice, palpitations or fainting promptly.
risks: Lung inflammation, which can be serious or fatal
Liver test changes and possible liver injury

logistics.title: Your practical tepotinib plan
logistics.intro: The usual starting dose is 450 mg once daily: two 225 mg tablets taken together with food. Treatment is continuous, without a planned rest week, while it is helping. Follow your prescribed dose; the team may use one 225 mg tablet or pause treatment for side effects.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the MET result, previous treatment, prescription, first review and contact number.

sections.title: Taking your tablets
sections.text: Take at the same time each day with food and swallow whole. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Do not double a dose. Ask your pharmacist if the timing is uncertain or if you vomit; do not take a replacement without advice. If swallowing is difficult, ask about the approved water-dispersion method.

sections.title: Supplies and reviews
sections.text: Arrange repeat prescriptions before tablets run out. Keep blood-test and review appointments. The tablet regimen itself needs no infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask why, what must recover, when review is due and who will authorise restarting. Do not change between one and two tablets yourself.

sections.title: At a change or stop
sections.text: Agree scans, symptom follow-up and the medicine plan. Continue the contraception and breastfeeding precautions for at least one week after the final dose.

evidence.heading: Evidence for this treatment
evidence.summary: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.
evidence.limitations: Single-arm evidence does not establish comparative survival benefit; first-line trial patients are outside this NCCP indication.

teachback: Can you explain why the MET result and previous treatment matter, how you take the tablets with food, what to do if a dose is missed, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the advanced-disease treatment aim, possible benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, daily tablets with food, swelling and bowel effects, serious lung/liver/heart risks, monitoring, pregnancy and fertility, and the right to reconsider.

support.title: Swelling and weight changes
support.text: Report swelling early and discuss changes in weight, movement or breathing. The team will assess the cause and agree treatment; do not start a water tablet or change tepotinib yourself.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Agree a diarrhoea treatment plan before starting. Begin the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal medicine at the first loose stool as instructed, and maintain fluids if able. Persistent diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Tepotinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Agree an as-needed anti-sickness plan with the team, including medicine-interaction and heart-rhythm checks; no routine infusion premedication is specified.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Ask the pharmacist to check all prescribed medicines, non-prescription medicines and supplements before changes. Tepotinib can affect medicines including dabigatran, digoxin, rosuvastatin and metformin. Supportive medicines may also affect heart rhythm; individual advice is needed.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose; women using hormonal contraception should also use a barrier method. Men with a partner who could become pregnant should use barrier contraception for the same period. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least one week afterwards. Human fertility effects are not known; discuss fertility before starting.

chapters.intro: VISION found that tepotinib could shrink some advanced MET exon 14 skipping lung cancers, including cancers previously treated with other medicines. It was a single-arm study, so it does not show how much longer people live compared with another treatment. Study results describe groups and cannot predict your own outcome.

items.title: Your own decision
items.text: Ask how closely the trial population matches your situation and discuss alternatives and remaining uncertainties.

chapters.title: When treatment changes
chapters.intro: The team authorises continuation, a pause, restart or stopping.

items.title: Review benefit and side effects
items.text: Agree who will review test results and confirm the dose. A source reduction to 225 mg is a clinician decision, not an instruction to halve tablets yourself.

items.title: Follow-up
items.text: Confirm the next treatment or follow-up plan, symptom advice and precautions after the final dose.

questions.q: Is this a fixed course of chemotherapy?
questions.a: No. These targeted tablets are taken daily without a planned rest week, while they are helping and your team considers treatment appropriate.

questions.q: Why does a trial mention 500 mg?
questions.a: The VISION trial’s 500 mg salt dose corresponds to 450 mg active tepotinib. The prescribed tablets contain 225 mg active tepotinib each; follow your own prescription.

questions.q: What if I forget or vomit a dose?
questions.a: Take a forgotten dose when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Never double up. Ask your pharmacist about vomiting or uncertain timing before taking any replacement.

questions.q: Why might my creatinine test change?
questions.a: Tepotinib can change how creatinine is handled by the kidneys, but real kidney problems can also occur. The team must assess the change; neither explanation should be assumed.

questions.q: Can I change the dose when I feel better?
questions.a: Only your team can authorise restarting or changing the dose after side effects. Feeling better does not establish that blood tests or other checks have recovered.
